methodological_rigor.justification: Retrospective single-center cohort of 160 HCC patients with CTC detection using Cyttel immunomagnetic bead enrichment + imFISH. The CTC-ALRI score is constructed from optimal ROC-derived cutoffs (ALRI 17.56, simplified to 18) and CTC>=1. Multivariable Cox regression identified CTC status and ALRI as independent RFS predictors; Fine-Gray competing risks analysis and landmark analysis (at 24 months) were performed. However, internally optimized cutoffs on the same cohort used for model building introduces optimism bias, acknowledged by authors. No independent validation cohort, sample size is modest (n=160), and bootstrap resampling provides only internal robustness. Ki-67 correlation analysis was performed on only 46 patients (28.75%).

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Individual cohort study with multivariable Cox analysis maps to Oxford LoE 2b. The score's reliance on routine blood parameters makes it highly accessible, particularly attractive for resource-limited settings. Reported AUCs of 0.725-0.729 for 1- and 2-year recurrence outperform tumor size, AFP, BCLC, TNM, ERASL, SSCLIP, and Korean models in the same cohort — clinically meaningful if externally validated. Actionable thresholds (score 2: 84% recurrence, median RFS 9.2 months) motivate intensive surveillance/adjuvant interventions.

reporting_quality.justification: As a multivariable prediction-model development study, TRIPOD is the applicable standard. Cohort definition, CTC detection protocol, ALRI calculation, multivariable model fitting, ROC/C-index, Fine-Gray competing risks, and landmark analyses are all described with reasonable clarity, and figure/table legends are detailed. However, TRIPOD is not cited, no checklist is provided, internal validation is limited to bootstrap on the same data (no split-sample or external validation), and no data/code availability statement is disclosed.

novelty_literature.justification: Individually CTCs and ALRI have been studied in HCC (refs 17, 18, 22, 23), but the authors position the CTC-ALRI composite score as the first integration of these two biomarkers. The differential recurrence-pattern finding (CTC predicts intrahepatic, ALRI predicts extrahepatic recurrence by Fine-Gray competing risks) is a genuinely interesting biological observation. The contribution is a meaningful combination/extension of existing markers rather than a fundamentally new biomarker.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is well written with a clear structure, thorough figure legends, and explicit caveats throughout (e.g., mechanistic interpretations are labeled hypothesis-generating, sample-size limitations for Ki-67 analysis are flagged). The Methods describe the landmark analysis approach explicitly to avoid guarantee-time bias, which reflects statistical rigor in presentation. Some sentences are overly long but overall polished.

key_strengths: Clear integration of CTC (tumor dissemination) and ALRI (liver injury + host immunity) into a single 0/1/2 score with stepwise RFS gradient (not reached / 39.2 / 9.2 months)
Fine-Gray competing risks analysis revealing differential prediction: CTC for intrahepatic, ALRI for extrahepatic recurrence
Properly designed landmark analysis at 24 months with explicit avoidance of guarantee-time bias
Head-to-head comparison against six established models (AFP, tumor size, BCLC, TNM, ERASL, SSCLIP, Korean) with superior AUC/C-index
Biological corroboration via Ki-67 gradient (in a subset) and clear acknowledgment of mechanism as speculative
key_concerns: Internally optimized cutoffs (ALRI 17.56, approximated to 18) on the same cohort used for model development — optimism bias acknowledged but not resolved
No independent external validation cohort — critical for a prediction model claim of superiority
Ki-67 analysis in only 46/160 patients (28.75%) limits biological validation
TRIPOD not cited and no data/code availability disclosed
Dichotomization of continuous variables (ALRI, CTC) acknowledged as information-loss limitation
chief_reviewer.rationale: A methodologically careful single-center cohort study proposing a novel composite biomarker (CTC-ALRI) with clear head-to-head advantage over established HCC recurrence models, but without external validation and with acknowledged internal-optimism bias; best fits a tier 3 specialty oncology journal after major revisions to add independent validation and explicit TRIPOD adherence.
